output.brief: Analyzer B looks fine. The single Level 2 potassium flag is most likely a chance outlier or a one-off sampling glitch. Evidence: the repeat on the same vial passed within 21 minutes, and Levels 1 and 3 were normal. Sodium and chloride were normal. There were no other QC rule violations in a month. Level 2 means are unchanged after the lot change (5.81 before, 5.80 after). Re-tested patient samples agree with Analyzer A (mean difference +0.02, all within limits). The patient median is stable. All scheduled QC ran on time, so the skipped-QC suspicion is not supported. The Ward 6 high potassiums are split evenly between Analyzers A and B (7 each). They coincide with the tube outage, since most high results had delays over 3 h, and with four renal overflow patients. Delayed transport is a likely cause, but that is not proven. What to sign off: return B to potassium service and close the review of the 186 flagged results with no amendments. Do not recall about 2,900 results or widen the limits. Quarantining the lot is not justified. Ask Ward 6 to repeat samples on fresh, promptly delivered specimens, and fix the tube station. Optionally add extra Level 2 QC for a week. I would not record the sampling glitch as the confirmed cause, because that is unproven. I am fairly confident in this. I did not collect further evidence.
